ITS.journal.journal_id: Primary key for the journal record. This is the internal ID used for joins to other tables (e.g. tbl_ebm.journal_id).
ITS.journal.old_journal_id: A legacy/previous journal ID from before a past system migration. Not populated for every journal (some are NULL). Do not use for current joins — journal_id is the current key.
ITS.journal.nid: An internal node/content ID (5-digit numeric). Not a foreign key to another table in this dataset — treat as an internal reference number, not a join key.
ITS.journal.publisher_id: Numeric ID identifying the journal's publisher. There is no separate publishers table in this dataset — publisher_name_dummy on this same table holds the readable publisher name for this ID.
ITS.journal.journal_type: Free-text label for whether the journal is Subscription or Open Access. Values: 'Subscription' or 'Open Access'. See jtype for the canonical coded version of the same fact — prefer jtype for filtering.
ITS.journal.jtype: The canonical coded column for subscription-vs-open-access status. S = Subscription, O = Open Access. Use this column (not journal_type or IsOpenAccess) when filtering or grouping by open access status, since it is the single-letter code the rest of the system treats as authoritative.
ITS.journal.title: The journal's full official name (e.g. 'Current Diabetes Reviews'). Use this for matching a journal by its full/complete name.
ITS.journal.subtitle: A longer descriptive subtitle for the journal, typically phrased as 'Research and Reviews in <title>'. Usually near-identical to journal_subtitle.
ITS.journal.old_subtitle: Legacy subtitle field from a previous system version. Always empty/NULL in current data — do not use, the real subtitle is in 'subtitle' or 'journal_subtitle'.
ITS.journal.jms_jcode: The journal's short code/abbreviation as used in the external JMS system (e.g. 'CMC', 'CDR'). Users very often refer to a journal by this short code instead of its full title; check this column (and abbrev_journal_title_dummy, which holds the same value) when a query mentions a short, all-caps or abbreviation-looking journal identifier.
ITS.journal.journal_subtitle: Same descriptive subtitle as 'subtitle' — the two columns are populated identically in this dataset. Either can be used.
ITS.journal.doi: The journal-level DOI prefix identifier (e.g. '10.1000/jms.00001'). Used for citation/indexing purposes, not typically what a user means by 'journal ID'.
ITS.journal.trendmd_id: An integration ID for the TrendMD content-recommendation service. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.price: The journal's standard subscription/access price, in the system's base currency. Same value as epub_price in this dataset.
ITS.journal.issn: The journal's print ISSN (International Standard Serial Number) — a unique identifier for the print edition.
ITS.journal.image_file_name: Filename of the journal's cover/thumbnail image asset. Not analytically meaningful — always 'journal.jpg' placeholder in this dataset.
ITS.journal.beta_image_file_name: Filename for an alternate/beta cover image. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.eissn: The journal's electronic ISSN (for the online edition), distinct from the print 'issn' column.
ITS.journal.epub_price: The journal's electronic/ePub access price. Same value as 'price' in this dataset — the two appear to track together.
ITS.journal.old_jour_id: Another legacy journal ID field from a prior system, duplicating old_journal_id's values. Not populated for every journal. Do not use for current joins.
ITS.journal.published: Whether the journal record itself has been published/finalized in the system. In this dataset every row is 1. Not the same concept as journal_status (overall active/inactive) or is_visible (public site visibility) — each tracks a different lifecycle flag.
ITS.journal.created: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) of when the journal record was created.
ITS.journal.created_by: Numeric user/staff ID of who created the journal record. No user-name lookup table is included in this dataset.
ITS.journal.updated_by: Numeric user/staff ID of who last updated the journal record.
ITS.journal.last_modified: Unix timestamp of the most recent modification to the journal record. In this dataset all journals share the same value, suggesting a bulk update rather than per-journal edit history.
ITS.journal.keyword: Semicolon-separated search keywords describing the journal's subject matter, derived from its title.
ITS.journal.description: A short marketing/summary description of the journal's scope, typically one sentence.
ITS.journal.catalog_desc: A very short catalog-listing description of the journal, e.g. '<title> — scholarly journal.' Used for compact listings rather than the full 'description'.
ITS.journal.formerly_title: The journal's previous name, if it was renamed. Always empty/NULL in current data — none of these journals have a recorded rename history.
ITS.journal.discount_offer: Text describing any active discount/promotional offer for the journal. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.editorial_policy: Free-text statement of the journal's editorial/ethical policy. Same boilerplate text across all journals in this dataset.
ITS.journal.guideline_for_reviewers: Free-text guidance given to peer reviewers for this journal. Same boilerplate text across all journals in this dataset.
ITS.journal.ifa: Unclear/legacy field, always empty/NULL in current data. Do not rely on this column for any analysis.
ITS.journal.aims_and_scope: Free-text statement of the journal's research aims and scope. Same boilerplate text across all journals in this dataset.
ITS.journal.flyer_aims_and_scope: A shortened aims-and-scope text intended for a promotional flyer. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.facebook_like_api_code: Legacy Facebook social-plugin integration code. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.jms_link: A URL linking to the journal's page in the external JMS system. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.impact_factor: The journal's current Impact Factor (a citation-based ranking metric), stored as text. Same value as org_impact_factor in this dataset.
ITS.journal.ranking_and_category: Free-text subject-area classification for the journal (e.g. 'Health Sciences; Research'). Same value across all journals in this dataset — likely a placeholder rather than a per-journal classification.
ITS.journal.eic_detail: Intended to hold detail/contact info about the journal's Editor-in-Chief. Always empty/NULL in current data — EIC identity should instead be found by joining tbl_ebm (filtered to the EIC role via tbl_ebm_role) to this journal's journal_id, not from this column.
ITS.journal.eic_detail_old: Legacy version of eic_detail from a prior system. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.scimago_journal_ranking: The journal's SCImago quartile ranking (Q1 = top quartile through Q4 = lowest). A recognized standard research-impact tier, distinct from impact_factor and ScopusCiteScore.
ITS.journal.flyer_link: URL to a downloadable promotional flyer for the journal. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.left_panel: CMS/website layout field for the journal's page left sidebar content. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.right_panel: CMS/website layout field for the journal's page right sidebar content. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.journal_submenus: CMS field listing the journal's website submenu structure. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.social_media_link: URL to the journal's social media presence. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.journal_insight_url: URL to an external analytics/insight dashboard for the journal. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.journal_on: Which platform hosts the journal's submission system. In this dataset always 'JMS' (the Journal Management System).
ITS.journal.journal_status: Overall active/inactive status of the journal record. Coded: 1 = active, 2 = not active. In this dataset all sampled journals are 1 (active). Distinct from 'published' (record publication state) and 'is_visible' (public site visibility) — each tracks a different lifecycle flag; do not use them interchangeably.
ITS.journal.journal_email: The journal's editorial contact email address, typically following an editorial@<code>.example.org pattern.
ITS.journal.signature: Intended to hold an email signature block for journal correspondence. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.manager_name: Name of the staff member who manages this journal internally (e.g. 'Manager A'). A small fixed set of internal managers, not the Editor-in-Chief.
ITS.journal.journal_banner: Filename/path for the journal's website banner image. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.IsOpenAccess: A second, separate open-access flag from 'jtype', coded as 0/1 (1 = open access) rather than S/O. Prefer 'jtype' as the canonical column for open-access filtering — this column is a denormalized duplicate and the two should be cross-checked rather than assumed identical if they ever appear to disagree.
ITS.journal.journal_rental: Whether per-article rental access is offered for this journal. In this dataset always 'N' (not offered).
ITS.journal.org_impact_factor: The journal's 'official'/organization-reported Impact Factor. Same value as 'impact_factor' in this dataset.
ITS.journal.ScopusCiteScore: The journal's Scopus CiteScore metric (a citation-based ranking similar to but distinct from Impact Factor), stored as text.
ITS.journal.ScopusCiteID: The journal's unique identifier within the Scopus database (e.g. 'SC431289'), used for citation/indexing lookups — not a join key within this dataset.
ITS.journal.continues_publication_journal: Whether the journal follows a volume-based continuous-publication (CP) model rather than discrete issues. Coded: 1 = yes (CP journal), 0 = no. In this dataset all sampled journals are 0.
ITS.journal.IsIssue: Whether the journal publishes in discrete numbered issues (as opposed to continuous publication). Coded: 1 = yes, 0 = no. In this dataset all sampled journals are 1.
ITS.journal.cp_volume_year: For continuous-publication journals, the current volume's year (e.g. 2024, 2025). Only meaningful in conjunction with continues_publication_journal = 1.
ITS.journal.cp_issue_journal: For continuous-publication journals, whether the journal is ALSO organized into issues within its CP volumes. Coded: 1 = yes, 0 = no. In this dataset all sampled journals are 0.
ITS.journal.ebm_flag: Whether this journal has an active Editorial Board Management (EBM) record set up, i.e. whether it participates in the tbl_ebm editor-tracking workflow. In this dataset always 1 (enabled).
ITS.journal.science_direct_line: Legacy integration field for a ScienceDirect content line. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.publisher_id_dummy: Duplicate of 'publisher_id', stored as text instead of a number. Use 'publisher_id' for numeric comparisons; this appears to be a denormalized/legacy copy.
ITS.journal.journal_id_dummy: Duplicate of 'journal_id', stored as text instead of a number. Use 'journal_id' (the real primary key) for joins — this is a denormalized/legacy copy, not a separate identifier.
ITS.journal.abbrev_journal_title_dummy: The journal's short code/abbreviation (e.g. 'CMC', 'CDR') — holds the same value as jms_jcode in this dataset. Users frequently refer to a journal by this short code rather than its full title; check this column when a query mentions a short, all-caps journal identifier instead of a full name.
ITS.journal.publisher_name_dummy: The readable name of the journal's publisher (e.g. 'Bentham Science Publishers'). Corresponds to publisher_id — use this column when a query asks about a publisher by name.
ITS.journal.googletags: Semicolon-separated SEO tags derived from the journal title, used for search-engine metadata. Not analytically meaningful beyond keyword search.
ITS.journal.ebm_data_status: Whether this journal's Editorial Board Management data has been synced/validated. In this dataset always 1.
ITS.journal.avg_first_decision_time: The journal's average time (in days) from manuscript submission to first editorial decision — a performance/turnaround metric.
ITS.journal.new_mps_journal: Whether the journal is live on the newer MPS publishing platform. Coded: 1 = live, 0 = not live.
ITS.journal.submission_link: Whether the manuscript submission link is turned on or off for this journal. Coded: 1 = on. In this dataset always 1 (on) — no sampled journal has it off.
ITS.journal.is_visible: Whether the journal is shown or hidden on the public-facing website. Coded: Y = shown, N = hidden. In this dataset always 'Y'. Distinct from 'journal_status' (internal active/inactive) and 'published' (record publication state) — a journal could in principle be active internally but hidden publicly, or vice versa.
ITS.journal.journal_sale: Whether the journal is marked as for-sale (a special pay-per-view/purchase program), coded 1 = not sale, 2 = sale. Note the polarity here does NOT match sale_journal_ppv/published/journal_status, where 1 is typically the positive/active state — double-check this specific column's mapping rather than assuming.
ITS.journal.sale_journal_banner_box: Banner/promotional content shown for a for-sale journal. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.sale_website_link: External sales page URL for a for-sale journal. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.sale_submission_link: Submission link specific to a for-sale journal's workflow. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.journal.sale_journal_ppv: For a for-sale journal, whether the pay-per-view price is displayed to readers. Coded: 1 = price shown, 2 = price not shown. Only meaningful when journal_sale = 2 (sale).

ITS.tbl_ebm.ebm_id: Primary key for this Editorial Board Management (EBM) record — i.e. one row represents one editor holding one role on one journal.
ITS.tbl_ebm.added_by: Numeric staff ID of who added this EBM record. No user-name lookup table is included in this dataset.
ITS.tbl_ebm.journal_id_jms: The journal ID as known in the external JMS system. Holds the same value as 'journal_id' in this dataset — use 'journal_id' for joins to the journal table.
ITS.tbl_ebm.journal_id: Foreign key to journal.journal_id — identifies which journal this editorial role belongs to. Use this column to join to the journal table.
ITS.tbl_ebm.editor_id: Foreign key to tbl_editors.editor_id — identifies which editor holds this role. Use this column to join to the editors table.
ITS.tbl_ebm.ebm_role_id: Foreign key to tbl_ebm_role.role_id — identifies which editorial role this record represents. Holds the same value as 'role_id' in this table.
ITS.tbl_ebm.role_id: Foreign key to tbl_ebm_role.role_id, duplicating ebm_role_id. Either column can be used to join to tbl_ebm_role.
ITS.tbl_ebm.region_id: Numeric ID for the editor's assigned geographic region for this role. No separate regions lookup table is included — 'section_region' on this same table holds the readable region name.
ITS.tbl_ebm.main_section: The broad subject-area section this editorial role covers (e.g. 'Chemistry', 'Clinical Medicine'). A small fixed set of top-level subject categories.
ITS.tbl_ebm.section: The specific sub-section or manuscript-type category this role covers within main_section (e.g. 'Reviews', 'Drug Discovery'). More granular than main_section.
ITS.tbl_ebm.ebm_role_name: The editorial role name as stored on this record (e.g. 'EIC', 'Section Editor'). Duplicates the role name found via the tbl_ebm_role join — kept here as a denormalized copy for convenience, but tbl_ebm_role.role/nicename is the canonical source if the two ever disagree.
ITS.tbl_ebm.conditional_ebm: Whether this editorial appointment is conditional/provisional rather than a standard confirmed appointment. Coded: Y = conditional, N = standard.
ITS.tbl_ebm.executive_ge: Whether this is an Executive Guest Editor appointment specifically (a distinct sub-type of guest editorship). Coded: Y = yes, N = no.
ITS.tbl_ebm.section_region: The readable geographic region name for this editorial role (e.g. 'Europe', 'Asia'). Corresponds to region_id.
ITS.tbl_ebm.acceptance_date: The date the editor accepted this role invitation. NULL for roles where the invitation is still pending/unaccepted — useful for accepted-vs-pending analysis.
ITS.tbl_ebm.acceptance_email_text: Boilerplate confirmation text logged when the editor accepted the role invitation. Same text for every accepted record in this dataset.
ITS.tbl_ebm.resign_date: The date the editor resigned from this role, if applicable. Populated only for a minority of records — most editors have not resigned (NULL here). Cross-reference with 'ebm_status' (Active/Resigned) rather than relying on this column alone to determine current status.
ITS.tbl_ebm.resign_email_text: Free-text notes logged at resignation. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_ebm.cv_content_type: MIME type of the editor's uploaded CV file for this role record (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Not analytically meaningful.
ITS.tbl_ebm.cv_name: Filename of the editor's uploaded CV for this role record. Not analytically meaningful — always a generic 'editor_cv.pdf' placeholder in this dataset.
ITS.tbl_ebm.cv_updated_on: Date the CV file on this record was last updated.
ITS.tbl_ebm.email_content_type: MIME type of the acceptance-email record (e.g. 'text/html'). Not analytically meaningful.
ITS.tbl_ebm.email_accp_name: Filename of the stored acceptance-email content. Not analytically meaningful.
ITS.tbl_ebm.email_accp_created_on: Date the acceptance email was generated/sent — closely tracks acceptance_date.
ITS.tbl_ebm.agreement_form_name: Filename of the editor's signed agreement form for this role. Not analytically meaningful.
ITS.tbl_ebm.agreement_form_content_type: MIME type of the agreement form file. Not analytically meaningful.
ITS.tbl_ebm.agreement_form_updated_on: Date the signed agreement form was uploaded/updated.
ITS.tbl_ebm.eic_approval: Approval status of this role appointment by the journal's Editor-in-Chief. In this dataset always 'Approved' — no pending/rejected examples present.
ITS.tbl_ebm.eic_approval_content_type: MIME type of any file attached to the EIC approval record. Not analytically meaningful.
ITS.tbl_ebm.eic_approval_updated_on: Date the EIC approval was recorded.
ITS.tbl_ebm.director_approval: Approval status of this role appointment by an editorial director (a second approval step beyond eic_approval). In this dataset always 'Approved'.
ITS.tbl_ebm.director_approval_content_type: MIME type of any file attached to the director approval record. Not analytically meaningful.
ITS.tbl_ebm.director_approval_updated_on: Date the director approval was recorded.
ITS.tbl_ebm.created_on: Unix timestamp of when this EBM record was created.
ITS.tbl_ebm.updated_by: Numeric staff ID of who last updated this EBM record.
ITS.tbl_ebm.updated_on: Date this EBM record was last updated.
ITS.tbl_ebm.ebm_status: The current status of this editor's appointment. Values: 'Active' or 'Resigned'. This is the most direct column for determining whether an editor currently holds a role — prefer it over inferring status from resign_date alone.
ITS.tbl_ebm.source: Internal data-lineage tag noting where this record originated. In this dataset always 'synthetic_from_journals_dataset' — not a business-meaningful field.
ITS.tbl_ebm.flag: A generic internal flag field. Always '0' in current data — no observed meaning to distinguish values; do not use for filtering unless a nonzero value is confirmed to appear.
ITS.tbl_ebm.editor_user_id: Duplicate of 'editor_id', referencing the same editor's user-level ID. Use 'editor_id' for joins to tbl_editors.

ITS.tbl_ebm_role.role_id: Primary key for this role definition row.
ITS.tbl_ebm_role.role: The editorial role name in its short/original form (e.g. 'Co-EIC', 'EIC'). Use this OR nicename when filtering by role name — both describe the same set of roles, just formatted differently.
ITS.tbl_ebm_role.nicename: The same role as 'role' but spelled out in full (e.g. 'Co Editor in Chief' instead of 'Co-EIC', 'Editor in Chief' instead of 'EIC'). Prefer matching against whichever form (role or nicename) the user's own wording resembles more closely.
ITS.tbl_ebm_role.priority: Numeric display/sort order for this role in editor listings — not a measure of seniority or importance, purely a UI ordering value.
ITS.tbl_ebm_role.jms_role_id: Foreign key referencing the equivalent role ID in the external JMS system. Not used for joins within this database — only relevant if cross-referencing against JMS.

ITS.tbl_editors.editor_id: Primary key for the editor record. This is the ID used for joins from tbl_ebm.editor_id.
ITS.tbl_editors.fname: The editor's first name (may include middle initials or suffixes bundled in for some records, e.g. 'Atta-ur-Rahman, FRS').
ITS.tbl_editors.mname: The editor's middle name or initial. Not populated for all editors.
ITS.tbl_editors.lname: The editor's last/family name. Not populated for all editors — some records have an unusual or missing surname format.
ITS.tbl_editors.degree: The editor's academic degree(s), e.g. 'PhD', 'MD, PhD'. May list multiple degrees comma-separated.
ITS.tbl_editors.titles: The editor's professional title/position (e.g. 'Professor and Researcher', 'Senior Research Scientist') — distinct from 'salutation' (a name-prefix honorific like 'Dr.').
ITS.tbl_editors.salutation: The honorific prefix used before the editor's name (e.g. 'Dr.'). In this dataset always 'Dr.'.
ITS.tbl_editors.suffix: A name suffix (e.g. 'Jr.', 'III'). Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.institute: The specific research institute or lab the editor is affiliated with — more specific than 'university', which names the parent institution.
ITS.tbl_editors.university: The editor's primary university/institutional affiliation. Broader than 'institute' — a university can encompass multiple institutes/departments.
ITS.tbl_editors.pharmaceutical: The editor's affiliated pharmaceutical-industry unit, if any. Only populated for a minority of editors (those with pharma-industry ties) — NULL for purely academic editors.
ITS.tbl_editors.company: The editor's affiliated company/commercial research center, if any. Only populated for a minority of editors — NULL for purely academic editors.
ITS.tbl_editors.department: The specific academic department within the editor's university/institute (e.g. 'Department of Pharmacology').
ITS.tbl_editors.laboratory: The specific lab the editor works in, if applicable. Only populated for a minority of editors.
ITS.tbl_editors.library: A library affiliation associated with the editor, if applicable. Only populated for a minority of editors — meaning within this dataset is not fully clear; treat as a minor/optional affiliation field.
ITS.tbl_editors.expertise: The editor's primary field of research expertise (e.g. 'Organic Chemistry', 'Public Health') — useful for matching editors to a subject area.
ITS.tbl_editors.h_index: The editor's h-index (a standard academic citation-impact metric), stored as text.
ITS.tbl_editors.orcid_id: The editor's ORCID identifier — a globally unique researcher ID used across academic platforms, not specific to this system.
ITS.tbl_editors.researcher_id: The editor's Web of Science ResearcherID (e.g. 'RID827277') — a different researcher-identification system from ORCID.
ITS.tbl_editors.research_gate: URL to the editor's ResearchGate profile.
ITS.tbl_editors.google_scholar: URL to the editor's Google Scholar citations profile.
ITS.tbl_editors.scopus_id: The editor's Scopus Author ID — yet another distinct researcher-identification system, separate from orcid_id and researcher_id.
ITS.tbl_editors.biography: A short auto-generated biography sentence summarizing the editor's field, derived from 'expertise'.
ITS.tbl_editors.address: A general address line for the editor, typically 'Research Center, <city>'. Not a full street address.
ITS.tbl_editors.state: The editor's state/province of affiliation. Frequently 'Unknown' for editors outside the US or where state doesn't apply.
ITS.tbl_editors.country: The editor's country of affiliation — a key column for geographic analysis of the editorial board.
ITS.tbl_editors.phone: The editor's contact phone number, in this dataset following a placeholder +1-555-... pattern.
ITS.tbl_editors.fax: The editor's fax number. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.mobile: The editor's mobile phone number, separate from 'phone'. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.we_chat_number: The editor's WeChat contact ID. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.alt_email: A secondary/alternate email address for the editor. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.url: A personal or professional website URL for the editor. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.cv_content_type: MIME type of the editor's uploaded CV file (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Not analytically meaningful.
ITS.tbl_editors.cv_name: Filename of the editor's uploaded CV. Not analytically meaningful — always a generic 'cv.pdf' placeholder in this dataset.
ITS.tbl_editors.profile_pic: Filename/path of the editor's profile picture. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.profile_pic_type: MIME type of the profile picture file. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.web_format: A legacy formatting flag for how the editor's profile renders on the website. Always empty/NULL in current data.
ITS.tbl_editors.added_by: Numeric staff ID of who added this editor record. No user-name lookup table is included in this dataset.
ITS.tbl_editors.created_on: Date the editor record was created.
ITS.tbl_editors.updated_by: Numeric staff ID of who last updated this editor record.
ITS.tbl_editors.updated_on: Date the editor record was last updated.
ITS.tbl_editors.status: The editor's account status. Coded: A = active, B = blocked, D = deleted. In this dataset all sampled editors are 'A' (active).
ITS.tbl_editors.institution_id: An internal institution reference code (e.g. 'INST0098'). No separate institutions lookup table is included in this dataset — treat as an identifier only, not a joinable key here.
